options.help: minimum Python version the output must run on [default: the version of the interpreter that will run it]
The interpreter to run on, or the environment holding it. A bare name that is neither, like `python3.14`, is found on `PATH`
A program to start the interpreter through, such as a debugger that has to be the process the program runs in

which runtime type-soundness checks to insert: `default`, `all` (adds the opt-in `parameters` entry checks), `none`, or a comma-separated subset of `generic-calls`, `projections`, `iterations`, `assignments`, `returns`, `arguments`, `parameters`
wrap every function with a `raises` clause in a runtime guard that fails when it raises something the clause does not include
leave a closure made inside a loop sharing the loop's one binding, as python does, instead of binding the values of the iteration it was made in
supply a `build:` stamp, as `NAME=VALUE`. repeatable. overrides whatever this build could have worked out for itself, which is what a CI job that knows its own commit wants
Compile every imported module to a native extension first
Run in the tree this staged instead of in the current directory
Measure which lines run, with coverage.py, and write them to PATH as an LCOV report
profile the program with cProfile and write the snapshot to PATH, as the `pstats` file `cProfile` writes (`.pstat`)
